title: Calisthenics hybrid upper/lower
author: Dan M
desc:
This programme was designed to build strength in the traditional weighted calisthenics exercises, with an upper body focus on dips and pull ups. Also key to the programme is core strength and stability, making use of a variety of movements to train the core. The lower body element is designed to be a more bodybuilding style approach, centred on machines as an alternative to free weighted options such as barbell squats, although these can be substituted where preferred.

The programme should be run using a basic double progression for all exercises. This means that you should work each week through the prescribed rep ranges until you reach the top of the range. On the next week you can add more weight and repeat. For progression in exercises such as the L-sit or other static holds, simply try to increase the time in the hold or add 1 additional set. Once you have reached the top end of the time range for all sets, then look to move to the more difficult variations of the movement.

ss.note: If unable to do pull-ups or dips then either use the pull-up/dip assist machine or bands to help you achieve the reps. Over time you can progress to bodyweight and eventually weighted pull-ups/dips.

ex.note: Add weight to this exercise either by using a dumbbell, a plate or a straight bar
This should be done on parallettes or anything that can raise you off the ground, i.e 2 benches/boxes or a dip attachment. This can then be progressed to doing them off the floor.
If you are already able to muscle up, you can swap this out for that exercise instead.
Hands closer to the feet will increase the difficulty, hands further away will decrease difficulty.

This can be performed either bi-laterally with 1 dumbbell in each hand or contralaterally, with one dumbbell held on the opposite side of the working leg. Pick one method and stick with it throughout.

ss.note: Reps are per side.
If unable to do pull-ups or dips then either use the pull-up/dip assist machine or bands to help you achieve the reps. Over time you can progress to bodyweight and eventually weighted pull-ups/dips.
